analysis_trace: Trial NCT07542821 is a NOT_YET_RECRUITING randomized parallel-group behavioral intervention trial in Chinese cancer survivors (breast, head/neck, colorectal, prostate) with fear of cancer recurrence (FCR). Three arms: education-only (active comparator), ConquerFear (6-session metacognition-based psychological training), and Healthy Lifestyle (6-session nutrition/exercise guidance). Primary endpoint: FCRI score change from baseline to 3 months post-intervention (5 months). Secondary: HADS (anxiety/depression) and VR-12 (quality of life) at same timepoint.

Evidence retrieved: Europe PMC search results for ConquerFear interventions (40784346, 36669845, 37489745), psychological interventions for FCR, and lifestyle interventions for cancer survivors. Direct evidence from ConquerFear-HK trial (Chinese survivors, metacognition-based, similar population) supports efficacy. Meta-analyses of psychological interventions for cancer survivors show small-to-moderate effect sizes for anxiety/depression (HADS) and quality of life. Lifestyle interventions show modest benefits for QOL.

Evidence-role assessment: ConquerFear-HK (40784346) - indirect_direction, same intervention type, Chinese population, FCRI endpoint; mismatch: different trial, completed vs planned. Meta-analyses (42311272, 42180058, 42149231) - indirect_direction for HADS and QOL endpoints; numeric_use_allowed: false for precise values, true for directional support.

Primary endpoint (FCRI): Based on ConquerFear-HK positive results and metacognition-based intervention efficacy in similar population, predict ConquerFear group shows greater reduction vs education. Healthy lifestyle group may show smaller effect. Direction: reduction (improvement).

Secondary-0 (HADS): Psychological interventions typically reduce anxiety/depression. Predict both active groups show improvement vs education, with ConquerFear likely larger effect. Direction: reduction.
Secondary-1 (VR-12 QOL): Both interventions expected to improve QOL. Lifestyle interventions have established QOL benefits. Direction: improvement (increase).

Uncertainties: Trial not yet recruiting; exact effect sizes unknown; group-specific comparisons not defined in contract; VR-12 normative data limited for Chinese cancer survivors. Confidence lowered due to lack of direct results.
Safety: Behavioral interventions generally low risk. No significant adverse events expected.

Meta-analyses of psychological interventions for cancer survivors show small-to-moderate effect sizes for anxiety/depression (HADS) and quality of life. Lifestyle interventions show modest benefits for QOL.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT07542821 is a randomized parallel-group trial evaluating ConquerFear (metacognitive psychological training) vs Healthy Lifestyle (nutrition/exercise guidance) vs Education-only control in cancer survivors with fear of cancer recurrence (FCR). Primary endpoint: FCRI score change from baseline to 3 months post-intervention (5 months). Secondary: HADS (anxiety/depression) and VR-12 (quality of life).

Evidence base: Retrieved ConquerFear-HK protocol (BMJ Open 2023, PMID 36669845) showing the same intervention structure in Chinese cancer survivors with FCRI as primary outcome and HADS/EORTC-QoL as secondary. Original ConquerFear trial (Butow et al., Psycho-Oncology 2017) demonstrated efficacy vs attention control with sustained FCRI reduction at 3 and 6 months post-therapy. Network meta-analysis (Sage 2024) ranks ConquerFear-HK highest (SUCRA 99.2%) for FCR reduction.

Evidence matching: ConquerFear-HK protocol matches current trial in population (Chinese/Mandarin-speaking cancer survivors), intervention (6-session metacognitive training), and outcomes (FCRI, HADS, QoL). The current trial adds a healthy lifestyle comparator arm not present in prior studies.

Effect size estimation: Original ConquerFear trial showed FCRI total score reduction of ~10 points (moderate-large effect, d~0.5-0.7) vs control at 3 months. Similar effects expected for ConquerFear group here. Healthy lifestyle interventions show smaller effects on FCR (typically d~0.2-0.3) based on exercise/nutrition RCTs in cancer survivors.

HADS prediction: ConquerFear-HK protocol lists HADS as secondary outcome; metacognitive interventions typically reduce anxiety/depression with small-moderate effects (d~0.3-0.5). Healthy lifestyle may improve HADS through physical health benefits but effect likely smaller (d~0.2-0.3).

VR-12 prediction: Limited direct evidence for VR-12 specifically in this population. Generic QoL measures (EORTC-QLQ-C30) in similar trials show small improvements with psychological interventions (d~0.2-0.4) and modest gains with lifestyle interventions. VR-12 physical/mental component scores expected to follow similar patterns.

Key uncertainties: (1) No published results for this specific trial as of cutoff; (2) Healthy lifestyle arm as active comparator is novel vs prior ConquerFear studies; (3) Stratified randomization based on baseline FCR may affect effect estimates; (4) VR-12 less commonly used than SF-36/EORTC in cancer QoL studies.
Safety: Behavioral interventions have minimal safety concerns. No serious adverse events expected.

Trial success prediction: Primary endpoint (FCRI) likely to favor ConquerFear over education control based on consistent prior evidence. Comparison with healthy lifestyle is uncertain. Secondary endpoints likely to show modest benefits favoring psychological intervention.

PMC Copyright notice PMCID: PMC9872480 PMID: 36669845 Abstract Introduction Fear of cancer recurrence (FCR) is a prevalent and frequently debilitating response to a cancer diagnosis, affecting a substantial proportion of cancer survivors. Approximately 30% of local Hong Kong Chinese cancer survivors in a recent survey reportedly experienced persistent high FCR over the first-year post-surgery. This was associated with lower levels of psychological well-being and quality of life. A manualised intervention (ConquerFear) developed primarily based on the Self-Regulatory Executive Function Model and the Rational Frame Theory, has been found to reduce FCR effectively among Caucasian cancer survivors. The intervention now has been adapted to a Chinese context; ConquerFear-HK. The primary aim of this study is to evaluate its efficacy vs a standard-survivorship-care control (BasicCancerCare) in FCR improvement in a randomised control trial (RCT). Methods and analysis In this RCT, using the sealed envelope method, 174 eligible Chinese cancer survivors will be randomised to either the ConquerFear-HK or BasicCancerCare intervention. Both interventions include six sessions over 10 weeks, which will be delivered via face to face or online by trained therapists. The ConquerFear-HK intervention incorporates value classification, metacognitive therapy, attentional training, detached mindfulness and psychoeducation; BasicCancerCare includes relaxation training, dietary and physical activity consultations. Participants will be assessed at prior randomisation (baseline; T0), immediately postintervention (T1), 3 months (T2) and 6 months postintervention (T3) on the measures of FCR (Fear of Cancer Recurrence Inventory) as a primary outcome; metacognition (30-item Metacognitions Quesionnaire) and cognitive attentional syndrome (Cognitive-attentional Syndrome Questionnaire) as process outcomes; psychological distress (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale), cancer-related distress (Chinese Impact of Events Scale), quality of life (European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Core Questionnaire) and treatment satisfaction are secondary outcomes. Ethics and dissemination Ethics approval has been obtained from HKU/HA HKW Institutional Review Board (ref: UW19-183). The patients/participants provide their written informed consent to participate in this study. The study results will be disseminated through international peer-review publications and conference presentations. Trial registration number NCT04568226 . Keywords: ONCOLOGY, Adult oncology, MENTAL HEALTH STRENGTHS AND LIMITATIONS OF THIS STUDY. A randomised controlled trial is used to evaluate the effectiveness of a culturally adapted metacognitive intervention for fear of cancer recurrence in Chinese settings. This study includes an active control condition offering standardised survivorship care. Intervention fidelity will be assessed and highly monitored. An unblinded randomised trial design is used. Our sample includes only local Chinese cancer survivors, limiting generalisability. analysis_trace: Trial NCT07542821 is a randomized parallel-group trial evaluating ConquerFear (metacognitive psychological training) vs Healthy Lifestyle (nutrition/exercise guidance) vs Education-only control in cancer survivors with fear of cancer recurrence (FCR). Primary endpoint: FCRI score change from baseline to 3 months post-intervention (5 months). Secondary: HADS (anxiety/depression) and VR-12 (quality of life).

Evidence base: Retrieved ConquerFear-HK protocol (BMJ Open 2023, PMID 36669845) showing the same intervention structure in Chinese cancer survivors with FCRI as primary outcome and HADS/EORTC-QoL as secondary. Original ConquerFear trial (Butow et al., Psycho-Oncology 2017) demonstrated efficacy vs attention control with sustained FCRI reduction at 3 and 6 months post-therapy. Network meta-analysis (Sage 2024) ranks ConquerFear-HK highest (SUCRA 99.2%) for FCR reduction.

Evidence matching: ConquerFear-HK protocol matches current trial in population (Chinese/Mandarin-speaking cancer survivors), intervention (6-session metacognitive training), and outcomes (FCRI, HADS, QoL). The current trial adds a healthy lifestyle comparator arm not present in prior studies.

Effect size estimation: Original ConquerFear trial showed FCRI total score reduction of ~10 points (moderate-large effect, d~0.5-0.7) vs control at 3 months. Similar effects expected for ConquerFear group here. Healthy lifestyle interventions show smaller effects on FCR (typically d~0.2-0.3) based on exercise/nutrition RCTs in cancer survivors.

HADS prediction: ConquerFear-HK protocol lists HADS as secondary outcome; metacognitive interventions typically reduce anxiety/depression with small-moderate effects (d~0.3-0.5). Healthy lifestyle may improve HADS through physical health benefits but effect likely smaller (d~0.2-0.3).

VR-12 prediction: Limited direct evidence for VR-12 specifically in this population. Generic QoL measures (EORTC-QLQ-C30) in similar trials show small improvements with psychological interventions (d~0.2-0.4) and modest gains with lifestyle interventions. VR-12 physical/mental component scores expected to follow similar patterns.

Key uncertainties: (1) No published results for this specific trial as of cutoff; (2) Healthy lifestyle arm as active comparator is novel vs prior ConquerFear studies; (3) Stratified randomization based on baseline FCR may affect effect estimates; (4) VR-12 less commonly used than SF-36/EORTC in cancer QoL studies.
Safety: Behavioral interventions have minimal safety concerns. No serious adverse events expected.

Trial success prediction: Primary endpoint (FCRI) likely to favor ConquerFear over education control based on consistent prior evidence. Comparison with healthy lifestyle is uncertain. Secondary endpoints likely to show modest benefits favoring psychological intervention.
